quotes.text: AI builder is a feature inside Microsoft Power Platform. It lets you create and use AI models to take over business tasks you'd normally do by hand.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Compact definition of AI Builder for beginners.

quotes.text: Most beginners assume custom always means better, and that assumption is wrong. Custom means more specific, and more specific is only better when your problem is specific to.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Corrects a common misconception about custom versus pre-built models.

quotes.text: You only need five documents to get started. Not five thousand, and not some labeled data set.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Shows how low the entry barrier for document processing is.

quotes.text: It's only as good as the history you feed it. And if your past data is messy or thin, the predictions will be messy too.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Honest caveat about prediction models and data quality.

quotes.text: Adding an AI builder action turns a flow into a premium flow. And if that flow lives inside an app, it makes the app a premium.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Licensing consequence teams should know before they build.

Where AI Builder fits in real work

takeaways: AI Builder adds task-focused AI models to Power Apps and Power Automate, so you can automate business chores without writing code.
Use pre-built models for common, generic problems and train custom models such as document processing when your documents or data are specific to your business.
Building and testing models is free, but running them in a live app or flow consumes credits and makes the flow or app premium.
hook: Many business users think AI needs engineers and months of setup. This Simply Explained episode is for Power Platform beginners who want to use AI Builder inside Power Apps and Power Automate. You will learn which models fit which tasks, how document processing and prediction work, and how credits and licensing affect your plans.
